chapter: Glen Island, early records and Duke Ellington
title: Ellington band members at the Cotton Club and Toby Hardwick's bass sax
summary: Barnet says he knew nearly everyone in Duke's band, and tells how Otto Hardwick kept an unplayed bass saxophone with a mirror to watch the showgirls.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah. Back to New York and the Cotton Club and Duke.
Who all did you know in the band well?

Well, I knew Barney and Johnny and Harry and Rex, and of course I knew Lawrence, but Lawrence was always the utmost -- the gentleman all the time and rather reserved, but a real nice fellow. And Tizol, Juan Tizol, we were very friendly with him, and Sonny. Of course

everybody that's met Sonny is his friend right off the bat. And -- well, let's see, Paul wasn't with the band yet there. Toby, Otto Hardwick, he and I became very good friends. I was practically friends with the whole band.

Oh, he was a doll. He drank a little too much, but who didn't, you know, in those days. Toby, you know, used to have that big bass saxophone beside him. I said, 'What have you got that thing there for?' And he said, 'Come up on the bandstand after we finish the set and I'll show you.' Well, they had the showgirls that came up there, around on a platform, around in back of the band and down the sides like that. He had a mirror fixed up on the saxophone, the bass saxophone, so he could see all the girls up there.
That's funny. I didn't know he had a bass saxophone on the stand.
Well, he did there, but he never played it.
I never heard him play it.
I asked him, I said, 'What have you got that thing for? You never touch it.'
I think he used to play one note. They

had one of those triad, button endings, and they made the -- he'd hit the bottom one and then Carney would hit the next one, and -- I think that's all, but he never actually played anything on it. At least then. He must have played it at one time, though, because you don't buy one of those things without having a use for it. It's a monster, you know.
